title: Globular Cluster NGC 1846

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble view shows a spherical swarm of hundreds of thousands of stars. Ageing bright stars glow in intense red and blue, while most of the middle-aged stars, several billion years old, look whitish. This is NGC 1846, a globular cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud's outer halo. That neighboring dwarf galaxy of the Milky Way is visible from the southern hemisphere.

Near the bottom center sits a faint green bubble that seems out of place. It is a planetary nebula, the aftermath of a star's death, and the burned-out central star shows inside it. Nobody is sure whether the bubble belongs to the cluster or just happens to sit in the same direction, though measurements of the motions of the cluster stars and the nebula's central star suggest it might be a member.
Many distant background galaxies of varied shapes and structures are scattered around the cluster. Seen toward the constellation Dorado, NGC 1846 is roughly 160,000 light-years away.

understand.summary: Hubble's ACS took this image. NASA shows F435W in blue, F555W in green and F814W in red.
understand.eye: The exposure totals 34 minutes and includes near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see.

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took the image in January 2006, using filters that isolate blue, green and infrared starlight. A globular cluster is a tightly bound, roughly spherical group of old stars held together by its own gravity.
sources: NASA release: NASA’s Hubble Finds Stellar Life and Death in a Globular Cluster
alt: A spherical cluster of red, blue and whitish stars, with a faint green bubble near the bottom center and distant galaxies scattered around.
